meta.titre: Advertising and Sales Promotion: informing, persuading and boosting sales
meta.sous_theme: Advertising media, benefits to the manufacturer and sales promotion methods

sections.contenu_markdown: A company launches a new bar of soap. Radio spots tell people it exists, posters near the market remind them, and free samples are handed out at the entrance. Some of these are advertising and some are sales promotion, and the GCE Commerce papers expect you to tell them apart, to choose a medium for a product and to explain what advertising does for the manufacturer. This course gives you the definitions, the media and a method for explanation questions.

items: A manufacturer makes goods that are sold to wholesalers, retailers or consumers.
A brand is a name or sign that identifies the goods of one producer.
Profit is what remains of the revenue after costs are paid.

sections.titre: Advertising, its media and sales promotion
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What advertising is

**Advertising** is a paid message sent through a medium to make people aware of goods or services and to encourage them to buy. Its aims are to **inform** (a new product exists), to **persuade** (this one is better), to **remind** customers and to **compete** with rival brands.

Advertising by one firm for its own goods is individual advertising. When several firms in one trade pay together, for example producers advertising a product they all make, it is **collective advertising**.

### Media

| Medium | Strength | Weakness |
|---|---|---|
| Newspapers and magazines | Detailed, permanent information; can be kept | Only readers see it |
| Radio | Reaches many people, including those who cannot read | Message is short-lived; no pictures |
| Television | Sound, pictures and movement | Costly; only viewers see it |
| Posters and billboards | Seen by passers-by; low cost | Little detail |
| Catalogues, brochures and leaflets | Detailed description of goods | Must be distributed |
| Internet and social media | Can target chosen groups; interactive | Needs access to the internet |

### Benefits and drawbacks for the manufacturer

**Benefits:** increases sales and market share; introduces a new product; builds brand loyalty; helps meet competition; higher sales may allow larger production at a lower unit cost.
**Drawbacks:** costs money and may raise prices; results are uncertain; false claims harm the firm's name.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must recommend a medium for a product
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the medium to the **product, the audience and the budget**. A tractor needs detailed information, so use a brochure or a specialist magazine. A cheap drink for everyone may use radio or posters. Always give the reason for your choice.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about short-term efforts to raise sales that are not advertising
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Sales promotion** uses short-term offers to raise sales quickly: **free samples**, **discount coupons**, **price reductions**, **bonus packs** (extra quantity at the same price), **competitions and prizes**, **demonstrations**, **displays in the shop** and **trade fairs**. It encourages customers to buy now, while advertising builds awareness over time.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question starts with 'explain' and names one group
variantes.contenu_markdown: Answer for the group named. For the manufacturer: give a benefit, say what it does for the firm and add a short example. Do not drift into benefits to consumers.

sections.enonce_markdown: A manufacturer sells 2,000 packets of biscuits a month at a profit of 600 FCFA per packet (before the cost of advertising). After a month of radio advertising costing 250,000 FCFA, sales rise to 2,600 packets. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in sales. (b) Calculate the net gain from the advertising. (c) Comment.

etapes.justification: The increase is the new sales minus the old sales.
Divide the increase by the original figure and multiply by 100.
Each extra packet gives the profit per packet.
Subtract the advertising cost from the extra profit.
A positive net gain means the advertising paid for itself in the first month; some benefit may continue later.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The campaign was worth its cost.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Sales rose by 30% and the net gain was 110,000 FCFA.** The advertising paid for itself and left a profit. Part of the effect may continue after the campaign, since customers remember the brand. A manager would still check that the rise was caused by the advertising and not by another factor such as a festival season.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A free sample is a form of advertising.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A free sample is a sales promotion method. Advertising is a paid message through a medium.
items.correction_markdown: Advertising informs and persuades through a medium; free samples, coupons and price reductions are sales promotion.

items.erreur_markdown: 'Advertising on radio is best for every product.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The best medium depends on the product, the audience and the budget. A detailed technical product needs a brochure or a magazine.
items.correction_markdown: Choose and justify: 'A brochure suits a tractor because buyers need detailed information.'

items.erreur_markdown: Writing benefits to the consumer in a question about the manufacturer
items.pourquoi_faux: The question names the manufacturer, so benefits to consumers earn no marks.
items.correction_markdown: Write benefits to the firm: more sales, a launch for a new product, brand loyalty, resistance to competition.

items.pourquoi_faux: Advertising costs money, and these costs may be added to prices. Large sales may lower unit costs, but there is no guarantee.
items.correction_markdown: Advertising can lower the unit cost if sales rise a lot, but it may also raise the price.

items.erreur_markdown: Confusing collective advertising with competitive advertising
items.pourquoi_faux: Collective advertising is paid for together by firms in one trade. Competitive advertising is one brand trying to win customers from another.
items.correction_markdown: Collective: shared by many producers. Competitive: one brand against rival brands.

items.enonce_markdown: Name a suitable advertising medium for each: (a) a detailed description of the technical features of a new generator for engineers; (b) an announcement of a one-day sale to people passing along a busy road. Give one reason each.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A **brochure or a specialist magazine**: it can give a detailed description that engineers can read and keep. (b) A **poster or billboard** (or a banner at the shop): passers-by see it immediately and the message is short.

items.enonce_markdown: A shoe seller sold 80 pairs a month at a profit of 4,000 FCFA per pair. After spending 90,000 FCFA on leaflets and posters, the sales rose to 110 pairs. Calculate the percentage increase in sales and the net gain.
items.solution_markdown:
Extra pairs $= 110 - 80 = 30$.

Percentage increase $= \frac{30}{80} \times 100 = 37.5\%$.

Extra profit $= 30 \times 4\,000 = 120\,000$ FCFA. Net gain $= 120\,000 - 90\,000 = 30\,000$ FCFA.

**Increase: 37.5%; net gain: 30,000 FCFA.**

items.enonce_markdown: A supermarket plans to promote a new brand of tea. (a) Explain two sales promotion methods it could use (6 marks). (b) State the difference between sales promotion and advertising (2 marks). (c) Give two drawbacks of advertising for a manufacturer (2 marks).
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Any two, 3 marks each: **free samples**, where shoppers taste the tea and may buy it (1 mark for the method, 1 for how it works, 1 for the effect on sales); **bonus pack**, an extra quantity at the same price, which pushes customers to buy now; **discount coupon**, which lowers the price for the customer who presents it; **in-store display or demonstration**.

(b) Advertising is a paid message through a medium that informs or persuades over time; sales promotion is a short-term offer that pushes people to buy now (2 marks).

(c) Any two: it is costly; it may raise prices; results are uncertain; false claims damage the firm's name (1 mark each).

items_markdown: Advertising is a paid message through a medium that informs, persuades or reminds; sales promotion is a short-term offer that pushes people to buy now.
Choose the medium by product, audience and budget: brochures and magazines give detail, radio reaches many, posters reach passers-by.
Benefits to the manufacturer: higher sales, a launch for new products, brand loyalty, a defence against competition, and possibly a lower unit cost.
Drawbacks: cost, possible higher prices, uncertain results and the risk of misleading claims.
Sales promotion methods: free samples, coupons, price reductions, bonus packs, competitions, demonstrations, displays and trade fairs.
Net gain from advertising = extra profit - cost of advertising.
